🇷🇺 Russia’s Geran-5 drone closes in on record 800 km/h - nears cruise missile speed
Russia’s jet-powered Geran-5 attack drones used in recent strikes on [Ukraine’s military-linked targets](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76171) has reached speeds nearing 800 km/h, according to air-monitoring data circulating online.
👉 Previous estimates put the speed maximum at around 600 km/h. 
Russia has either upgraded existing models or fielded a new varia[nt still listed under the Geran-5 designation](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75584), analysts speculate.
🔶 speed increase means less time to detect drone threat, pass targeting data, and launch interceptors
🔶 countering made especially difficult for mobile fire teams & units optimized against slower UAVs
🔶 at roughly 800 km/h, the drone approaches the performance of some subsonic air-launched cruise missiles like [Russia’s Kh-101 ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72880)
🔶 it retains lower cost and mass-production potential of an unmanned system
Russia has progressively upgraded[ the Geran family with improved navigation](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74638), electronic warfare resistance and greater performance.
The Geran-5 model: 
🔴 uses a turbojet engine, unlike earlier piston-engine models
🔴 can carry a warhead weighing up to 90 kg
🔴 has an estimated operational range of ~1,000 km
🔴 at ~ 6 meters long, it uses cruise missile-style configuration rather than flying-wing design

📍 Israel’s ruling parties target Arab polling stations as Palestinian votes could decide who rules next
Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism parties plan to station nearly 2,000 activists as observers at polls in Arab areas in the Oct.27 Knesset elections, according to The Times of Israel.
👉 The deployment is ostensibly needed to flag irregularities in voting and counting - despite Israel’s Central Elections Committee maintaining that electoral fraud, if it occurs, is marginal. 
Critics speculate the move is designed to intimidate Palestinians with Israeli citizenship. Likud fears a strong turnout among Palestinians could tip the election against Netanyahu. The party has already failed in its bid to disqualify the two main Palestinian-led lists, Ra’am and the Joint List, which polls project may win around 14 seats combined. 
Since neithe[r Netanyahu’s coalition](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74575) nor the main Jewish opposition parties are expected to secure the 61 seats needed for a majority on their own, that makes Arab turnout a potential game-changer.
🔶 [Ra’am helped tip the balance](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73223) toward an anti-Netanyahu government in the 2021–22 coalition
🔶 Likud placed cameras in Arab communities in 2019 in a move widely seen as an attempt to deter voters
🔶 Netanyahu rallied his base in 2015 by warning that Arab voters were “heading to the polls in droves”
🔶 opposition figures, including Naftali Bennett, have since pledged to form a Zionist unity government without relying on Palestinian parties

In three cases, the objects were confirmed to be Hezbollah devices but Israel only managed to bring down one. events.text:
🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia scrambles for new trade lifeline to dodge Hormuz and Red Sea risks
Struggling to fend off [mounting risks to its maritime trade and energy infrastructure](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76242), Saudi Arabia is exploring expanding a new freight corridor, reports The Cradle.
👉 Saudi Arabia’s Port of NEOM and logistics partner CEVA Almajdouie have signed an MoU to study a combined sea-and-land freight corridor from Europe via Egypt and Saudi Arabia to Gulf Cooperation Council states and Iraq.
With shipping in the Strait of Hormuz disrupted, and Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea export terminals and East–West Pipeline pumping stations vulnerable to [Ansar Allah strikes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76201), the new route would link NEOM’s Red Sea port directly with CEVA Almajdouie’s land transport network.
♦️ cargo could be moved inland across Saudi Arabia and neighboring markets
♦️ maritime gateways would link up directly to high-capacity inland networks - essential for supply-chain resilience
♦️ for Iraq, the corridor would offer an alternative path for European and other imports, reducing dependence on conventional Persian Gulf routes
The project remains at an early exploratory stage, with no details yet released on costs, timelines or expected cargo volumes.

events.text:
🇰🇷🇺🇸 South Korea-US alliance frays at the edges amid trust issues
Intelligence restrictions, scaled-back military drills and disputes over investments are increasingly straining US-South Korea ties, reports Bloomberg.
👉 Tensions over intel cooperation date back to March, when Seoul’s unification minister publicly identified Kusong as the site of a North Korean uranium-enrichment facility.
The US reportedly viewed the disclosure as a breach of classified US intelligence and subsequently restricted some satellite-derived information on North Korea’s nuclear facilities. 
South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung rejected the allegations as “absurd.” 
South Korean officials insist that intelligence sharing on missiles, conventional forces and immediate military threats remains intact.
Other key flashpoints:
🔴 South Korean lawmaker Jung Chung-rae was forced to switch his planned US trip this month after his visa remained under review by the State Department and was not issued in time for a parliamentary audit of South Korean missions in the Americas. 
🔴 Donald Trump ordered a scaling back of the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield joint exercises in August from 11 days to five, with some live-fire and field training reduced or canceled. Trump cited costs, South Korea’s refusal to support US efforts against Iran, and claimed the drills sent an “inappropriate and hostile” signal to North Korea. 
🔴 Investment disputes: Disagreements persist over a $350 billion investment framework, including projects involving Alaska LNG and nuclear reactors. South Korea has insisted on commercial viability and domestic legal requirements, with some projects remaining under review.

🪖 Houthis flex clout, slam Aden palace with missiles as Saudi targets burn
Ansar Allah claimed responsibility for [the attack on the Al-Maashiq Palace complex](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76253), the seat of Yemen’s Saudi-backed government in Aden.
Houthi missiles and drones targeted what military spokesperson Yahya Saree said housed a “Saudi war operations room.” He declared any Saudi military or economic presence on Yemeni soil a legitimate objective. 
🔴 the site housed Saudi officers and weapons depots, according to the Houthi-run news agency SABA
🔴 assault killed five people and wounded 16, including guards and civilian staff
🔴 the prime minister was reportedly unhurt in the attack
The assault marked the first direct hit on the palace in the current phase of fighting.
The Saudi-led coalition detailed the scale of recent Houthi operations against the kingdom:
🔴 20 attacks this month on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, killing 17 and wounding 333
🔴 strikes on Abha airport that killed three and injured 28
🔴 intercepted drones over southern cities including Khamis Mushait
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the Houthis now field advanced ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats, supplied with help from regional actors.
